items.title: CMB.Tech Q3 profit $373.9m; Stolt-pool chemical tankers at $18,756/day so far in Q4
items.summary: CMB.Tech reported Q3 2026 net profit of $373.9m ($1.29/share) on revenue of $802.9m, against $17.3m a year earlier, and declared $0.65/share. Its 25k dwt stainless chemical tankers in the Stolt pool earned $21,601/day in Q3 and $18,756/day quarter-to-date in Q4, while VLCC spot has booked $635,199/day for 59% of Q4 days.

items.title: Kpler: USG–UKC MR rate down 40% on the week to $6.81/bbl
items.summary: Kpler's Nov 20 freight note puts TC14 (US Gulf–UK Continent MR) at $6.81/bbl, down $4.61 week on week, and TC2 (UKC–USAC MR) at $3.44/bbl, down $0.27. Korea–Singapore MR (TC11) fell $1.28 to $4.19/bbl, while MEG–Japan LR2 (TC1) rose $0.83 to $26.58/bbl after a Nov 13 low of $25.66.

items.title: IC Shipbrokers: product tanker rates easing on slower activity
items.summary: IC Shipbrokers' weekly report dated Nov 24 says product tanker fixing slowed and rates edged lower across loading areas, while crude tanker activity and rates were largely stable. The report gives no route-level figures.

items.title: EU proposes ban on Russian-insured tankers in 22nd sanctions package
items.summary: European Commission President von der Leyen outlined on Nov 23 a package that would bar tankers insured in Russia, stop EU firms from servicing Russian energy infrastructure including refineries, and add more than 70 vessels to the shadow-fleet list. It needs unanimous approval from all 27 member states. S&P data showed no oil or chemical tankers discharging in the Netherlands in November carried Russian cover.

items.title: Week 47: Baltic clean index 2,581; one-year MR charter $34,000/day
items.summary: Compass Maritime's Nov 23 report puts the Baltic Clean Tanker Index at 2,581, against 2,592 a week earlier and 811 a year ago, while the dirty index rose to 5,081 from 4,483. Its one-year time-charter assessment for MRs eased to $34,000/day from $36,500, with LR1s unchanged at $53,500 and VLCCs down to $184,500 from $234,000.

items.title: Jones Act waiver extended a third time, to cargoes loaded by Feb 14
items.summary: DHS has extended the Jones Act waiver for 90 days from Nov 16; covered products must be loaded by 11:59 pm ET on Feb 14, 2027. The list of 237 HTS codes is unchanged and includes crude, refined products, LPG/LNG, fertilizers, ethyl alcohol for fuel, sulfur-based chemicals, anhydrous ammonia and biodiesel; the vessel-availability and reporting steps also stay the same.

items.title: Houthis target Saudi Red Sea ports; projectile hits Jazan with minor damage
items.summary: The Saudi-led coalition said a Houthi projectile struck Jazan port on Nov 25, causing minor damage and no civilian injuries, and a drone was intercepted near Jeddah Islamic Port. On Nov 26 Saudi forces reported intercepting two ballistic missiles aimed at Riyadh, a cruise missile toward the western region and drones over the Eastern Province. The Houthis describe the strikes as retaliation for coalition attacks on Hodeidah.

items.title: Gulf: two tanker incidents off the UAE on Nov 25; crews safe
items.summary: UKMTO logged an explosion, believed to be an unidentified projectile, about 50 nm west of Dubai at 21:30 GMT on Nov 25; the tanker, not named, reported no damage. Separately, a Liberia-flagged tanker was hit about 14 nm northwest of Ras Al Khaimah, causing an engine-room fire; all 22 crew were reported safe.

items.title: Hormuz attack tally: 31 in October, about 19 in November through Nov 18
items.summary: UKMTO counts 31 attacks in and around the Strait of Hormuz in October and about 19 in November as of Nov 18, against 53 incidents from March to September. Most attacked tankers were in the southern part of the strait near Oman. The US blockade of Iran-linked shipping has been in place since April 13.

items.title: Swedish Club advises avoiding non-essential Hormuz transits
items.summary: P&I insurer the Swedish Club has urged members to avoid non-essential transits of the Strait of Hormuz as security deteriorates; gCaptain also reports four more vessels attacked in and around the strait, with Iran widening its actions to tugboats.

items.title: Lower Mississippi at New Orleans: safety zone in place through Dec 11
items.summary: The Coast Guard has set a one-mile safety zone (mile 95.5–96.5) for salvage of the capsized cruise vessel American Heritage, struck by the asphalt tanker Atlantic Asphalt on Nov 13. Limited two-way traffic is allowed through the Crescent City Connection main span, but deep-draft ships and tows of 10 or more barges move one-way; the alternate channel remains closed.

items.title: Houston Ship Channel: deep-draft transits up 12% in October
items.summary: Port Houston's November report shows 1,628 deep-draft transits in October (up 12% year on year) and 19,251 barge transits (down 2%). September foreign tonnage was 22.3m short tons, up 13%, with exports up 16%; the region handled 32% of US crude exports through September. Port Houston's terminals moved a record 415,326 TEU in October, up 14%.

items.title: Wednesday Nov 25 close: Dow 50,182.95 (+0.33%), S&P 500 7,182.78 (−0.25%), Nasdaq 23,585.80 (−0.62%)
items.summary: The Dow gained 164.25 points, the S&P 500 lost 18.31 and the Nasdaq 147.73, after indexes recovered most of a steep early decline led by chip stocks; the Russell 2000 rose 0.71% to 2,704.06. Nvidia closed down 3.9% at $149.30 after S&P Global Ratings warned of a possible downgrade. US markets are closed Thursday for Thanksgiving and reopen Friday for a shortened session.
items.source: Yahoo Finance / AP via BNN Bloomberg

items.title: Oil: Brent settles $94.61 (+3.5%), WTI $83.68 (+2.0%)
items.summary: Brent rose $3.21 and WTI $1.63 on Nov 25 after the Houthis claimed strikes on Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery and Riyadh. EIA data showed US crude stocks up 1.1 million barrels to 418.9 million in the week to Nov 20; OPEC+ meets Nov 29 to set 2027 output.

items.title: US natural gas: December Nymex closed $3.323/MMBtu on Nov 24
items.summary: The December contract rose 13.9 cents (4.4%) on Tuesday after falling 22.7 cents to $3.184 on Monday, per EBW Analytics. Henry Hub spot was near $3.30, and the consensus for this week's EIA storage report is a 17–25 Bcf draw.

items.title: Core PCE 3.3% in October; futures price about 98% odds of a December Fed hike
items.summary: Core PCE inflation rose to 3.3% year on year in October, above the 3.2% expected. Fed funds futures implied about a 98% chance of a 25 bp increase at the December meeting; the Beige Book noted continued cost pressures in energy, transportation, insurance and tariff-related expenses. Yahoo's quote showed the 10-year Treasury yield at 4.848%, down 5.6 bp, and Freddie Mac's 30-year mortgage average at 7.21%.

items.title: US announces new tariffs on China, EU and other partners
items.summary: The administration unveiled new tariffs of up to 20% on China, the EU and other trading partners, layered on existing rates and taking effect after a comment period, in January at the earliest. South Korean coverage says the 15% cap under the 2025 Korea–US deal remains for now.

items.title: Thursday: Europe and Asia higher; dollar at 159.14 yen
items.summary: In early Nov 26 trading the DAX was up 1.8% at 25,131.36, the CAC 40 up 1.6% and the FTSE 100 up 1.3% at 10,563.62. The Nikkei 225 gained 0.9% to 57,499.16, the Hang Seng 1.2% and the Kospi 0.3% after a 6.2% drop on Wednesday. The euro was at $1.0975.

items.title: Zelenskyy: Kyiv waiting for US to set date for next peace talks
items.summary: President Zelenskyy said Ukraine awaits a US-proposed date for the next round of talks with Russia, which he said should include Europe. The last US-mediated round was in Abu Dhabi on Nov 10–11; Moscow has opposed European participation and says no meeting with Europeans has been agreed.

items.title: Ukraine says it struck a Russian air base, damaging five aircraft
items.summary: Ukraine's General Staff said on Nov 25 its forces hit a major Russian air base and damaged five aircraft used in missile and bomb attacks on Ukraine. The claim has not been independently confirmed.

items.title: Merz tells Bundestag Russia poses a growing threat
items.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz defended higher defense spending and continued aid to Ukraine, telling parliament the threat from Russia is increasing. Separately, German defense officials are discussing how to offset a planned US military drawdown in Europe, according to POLITICO.

items.title: BBC analysis of leaked records puts Russian military deaths at 490,334 or more
items.summary: A BBC analysis of leaked Russian statistics estimates at least 490,334 Russian military deaths since 2022, drawing on more than 11 million death records reportedly obtained in a hack. Russia does not publish comparable figures.

items.title: US pauses joint military operations with Ecuador
items.summary: The administration has paused joint operations with Ecuador while it reviews a Sept 23 Ecuadorian raid that killed Carlos Germán Muñoz Jara; US officials say American forces did not take part.

items.title: Indonesia: mine flood in West Java leaves 8 dead, 18 trapped
items.summary: Indonesia's search and rescue agency said eight people died and 18 remained trapped after a mine flooded in West Java on Nov 25.

items.title: Broncos (8–2) at Steelers (6–4) Friday, 2:00 pm CT on Prime Video
items.summary: Denver is tied with Kansas City at 8–2 atop the AFC West, holds the division tiebreaker and is No. 2 in the AFC after beating Las Vegas 38–24 on Nov 22. Pittsburgh is 4–0 at home. ESPN lists RB J.K. Dobbins out (personal) and S Taylor Rapp questionable.

items.title: Texans (4–6) host Ravens (4–7) Sunday at noon CT on CBS
items.summary: Houston is second in the AFC South behind Jacksonville (7–3) and ninth in the AFC after a 26–3 win over Indianapolis on Nov 19. Baltimore QB Lamar Jackson is on injured reserve; for Houston, WR Marvin Harrison Jr. and DE Danielle Hunter are listed questionable.

items.title: Davis Cup: Italy edges South Korea 2–1, meets Czechia in Friday's semifinal
items.summary: After Musetti won the opening rubber 6–0, 7–6(5), Kwon Soon-woo beat Flavio Cobolli 3–6, 7–6(3), 7–6(5) to level the tie; Vavassori and Berrettini then won the doubles 7–6(2), 7–6(11). Germany–Great Britain and Austria–Spain quarterfinals are scheduled for Thursday in Bologna.
